why.title: Why I built this
why.description: The motivation and philosophy behind this project
why.problemIntro: Once you have a big collection of AV codes, you'll probably run into these:
why.problem1: Video sites keep changing domains or shutting down, breaking your saved links
why.problem2: Collections scattered across platforms are hard to manage
why.problem3: Sharing a list is awkward when everyone uses a different site
why.problem4: There's no simple way to organize and search your collection
why.solutionIntro: This project puts the code first, so you can:
why.solution1: Save only the codes, independent of any specific site
why.solution2: Move between video sites whenever you like
why.solution3: Share a code list and let friends pick their own site
why.solution4: Create as many playlists as you need
why.tech: Built with Next.js 15. Works without signing in.

recentOpens.title: How Recently opened works
recentOpens.description: Use the Recent tab as your starting point: open videos from there, then pick which ones to keep
recentOpens.step1: On the Recent tab, type a code or paste a URL and pick a source. "Open in …" from Explore, a shared playlist or any code's link menu works too. The code is remembered automatically (copying a single code's link counts as well).
recentOpens.step2: When you come back, a prompt at the bottom says "You opened N codes. Save them?", counting only codes not in a playlist yet. It takes you to the Recent tab; tap ✕ to hide it for now.
recentOpens.step3: The Recent tab lists what you opened. New codes are checked; codes already saved are marked "In a playlist".
recentOpens.step4: Tap "Add to playlist" and create a new playlist ("Recently watched" by default) or add to an existing one; duplicates are skipped.
recentOpens.privacy: The list stays on this device: never synced, backed up or counted in stats. Up to 100 entries, removed after 7 days, and you can clear it any time.
recentOpens.limit: The site only sees links opened from here, not what you click inside the video site, and it doesn't track watch time. For those, paste the URLs into a playlist's Add dialog and the codes are extracted for you.
